“The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.” In response, the FOMC cut the federal funds rate to the effective lower bound and launched large-scale purchases of Treasuries and MBS, expanded repo operations, eased discount window terms, and coordinated dollar swap lines. Consistent with the credit view and bank-lending channel literature (e.g., Oliner and Rudebusch; Gertler and Gilchrist), such measures can lower the external finance premium and help stabilize business fixed investment and household spending. With market-based inflation compensation falling, deflation risk rises; insights from inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson) and liquidity-trap analyses support aggressive easing and balance-sheet policies to anchor expectations near 2 percent. Overall sentiment remains negative due to the sharp real shock, but policy actions materially mitigate financial amplification and near-term downside risks.
